hook.en: Think of the nephron as a factory line. The first section recovers almost everything useful, the next ones fine-tune water and salt. Let us walk along it.
hook.kn: ನೆಫ್ರಾನ್ ಅನ್ನು ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆಯ ಸಾಲಿನಂತೆ ಯೋಚಿಸಿ. ಮೊದಲ ಭಾಗ ಉಪಯುಕ್ತವಾದುದನ್ನೆಲ್ಲಾ ಹಿಂಪಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ, ನಂತರದ ಭಾಗಗಳು ನೀರು ಮತ್ತು ಲವಣವನ್ನು ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮವಾಗಿ ಹೊಂದಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

Explain why the descending and ascending limbs behave differently

narration.en: Think of the nephron as a factory line. The first section recovers almost everything useful, the next ones fine-tune water and salt. Let us walk along it.
narration.kn: ನೆಫ್ರಾನ್ ಅನ್ನು ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆಯ ಸಾಲಿನಂತೆ ಯೋಚಿಸಿ. ಮೊದಲ ಭಾಗ ಉಪಯುಕ್ತವಾದುದನ್ನೆಲ್ಲಾ ಹಿಂಪಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ, ನಂತರದ ಭಾಗಗಳು ನೀರು ಮತ್ತು ಲವಣವನ್ನು ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮವಾಗಿ ಹೊಂದಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: The proximal convoluted tubule is lined by simple cuboidal brush-border epithelium, which increases the surface area for reabsorption. Nearly all essential nutrients and 70–80 per cent of electrolytes and water are reabsorbed here. The PCT also maintains pH and ionic balance by selectively secreting hydrogen ions and ammonia into the filtrate and absorbing HCO3− from it. In Henle's loop, reabsorption is minimal in the ascending limb but the loop maintains the high osmolarity of the medullary interstitial fluid. The descending limb is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes, so the filtrate becomes concentrated as it moves down. The ascending limb is impermeable to water but allows transport of electrolytes actively or passively, so the filtrate becomes dilute as it moves up.
body.kn: PCT ಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬ್ರಷ್ ಅಂಚಿನ ಘನಾಕಾರದ ಎಪಿತೀಲಿಯಮ್ ಇದ್ದು ಬಹುತೇಕ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಪೋಷಕಾಂಶಗಳು ಮತ್ತು 70–80% ವಿದ್ಯುದ್ವಿಭಾಜ್ಯಗಳು ಹಾಗೂ ನೀರು ಮರುಹೀರಲ್ಪಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಹೆನ್ಲೆಯ ಇಳಿಯುವ ಭುಜ ನೀರಿಗೆ ಪ್ರವೇಶ್ಯ, ಏರುವ ಭುಜ ನೀರಿಗೆ ಅಪ್ರವೇಶ್ಯ ಆದರೆ ವಿದ್ಯುದ್ವಿಭಾಜ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ಸಾಗಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: PCT: nutrients + 70–80% of water and electrolytes; secretes H+ and NH3
Descending limb: water out → filtrate concentrated
Ascending limb: salts out, water stays → filtrate dilute

narration.en: The teacher tabulates what each tubule segment does, draws the loop of Henle with water and salt movements, and shows pH balance in a tubule cell.

say.en: Each part of the tubule has its own job. The PCT does most of the reabsorption.
Henle’s loop and the later segments fine-tune the filtrate.
Watch the loop. The descending limb lets water out, so the filtrate concentrates. The ascending limb pumps salts out but keeps water, so the filtrate dilutes.
The PCT and DCT also keep blood pH right: they secrete H⁺ and ammonia into the filtrate and return bicarbonate to the blood.

Permeable to water, almost impermeable to electrolytes

explanation.en: The filtrate is concentrated as it goes down the descending limb and diluted as it goes up the ascending limb. The PCT, DCT and collecting duct also help keep the pH and ionic balance of the blood.

body.en: In the distal convoluted tubule, conditional reabsorption of Na+ and water takes place. The DCT can also reabsorb HCO3− and selectively secrete hydrogen and potassium ions and NH3 to maintain the pH and sodium–potassium balance of blood. The long collecting duct extends from the cortex to the inner parts of the medulla. Large amounts of water can be reabsorbed here to produce concentrated urine. It also lets small amounts of urea pass into the medullary interstitium to keep up its osmolarity, and it helps maintain pH and ionic balance by selectively secreting H+ and K+ ions.
body.kn: DCT ಯಲ್ಲಿ Na+ ಮತ್ತು ನೀರಿನ ಷರತ್ತುಬದ್ಧ ಮರುಹೀರಿಕೆ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ; H+, K+ ಮತ್ತು NH3 ಸ್ರವಿಸಲ್ಪಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಸಂಗ್ರಹ ನಾಳದಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ನೀರು ಮರುಹೀರಲ್ಪಟ್ಟು ಸಾಂದ್ರ ಮೂತ್ರ ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಯೂರಿಯಾ ಮೆಡುಲ್ಲಾದ ಅಂತರಾಳಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: DCT: conditional Na+ and water reabsorption; secretes H+, K+, NH3
Collecting duct: large water reabsorption; urea into medulla

The long collecting duct extends from the cortex to the inner parts of the medulla. Large amounts of water can be reabsorbed here to produce concentrated urine. It also lets small amounts of urea pass into the medullary interstitium to keep up its osmolarity, and it helps maintain pH and ionic balance by selectively secreting H+ and K+ ions.

problem.en: A sample of filtrate is collected at three points: the end of the PCT, the tip of Henle's loop and the beginning of the DCT. Predict whether it is isotonic, hypertonic or hypotonic to blood plasma at each point.

steps.en: PCT reabsorbs solutes and water in proportion, so the filtrate at its end is about isotonic.
The descending limb loses water but keeps electrolytes, so the filtrate becomes hypertonic towards the tip of the loop.
The ascending limb loses electrolytes but no water, so by the beginning of the DCT the filtrate is hypotonic.

body.en: The Descending limb lets water out (water leaves the tubule); the Ascending limb lets salts out. Never both in one limb.
